clue.text: Sailor Bill taking taxi back for game

indicators.note: back tells us to read the whole string of sailor, bill and taxi from right to left

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
AC is short for account, a bill
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A sailor called Bill takes a taxi back to play a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole run TARACCAB around.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a card game played in casinos.

clue.text: Plant some trees in Africa to shoot up

indicators.note: in a down clue, shooting up means reading the letters bottom to top
some of the words trees in Africa supply a run of letters

explanation.surface: Instructions to plant trees in Africa that will grow fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ESINA from 'treES IN Africa'; 'to shoot up' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anise is an aromatic herb grown for its liquorice-flavoured seeds.

clue.text: What sounds like sweet treat, a slab making you quite full

indicators.note: signals that a word is spelt by its pronunciation rather than written form

parts.note: choc is short for a chocolate, a sweet treat
a block is a slab

explanation.surface: A slab of chocolate as a treat that leaves you stuffed.
explanation.definitionFit: Crammed to the limit; packed tight with no space left, as a crowded room might be.

clue.text: Think back about someone in the club?

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a club's people are its members

explanation.surface: Reflecting on a club associate.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall the past is to bring it back to mind.

clue.text: One militant star wielded iron maybe

indicators.note: a weapon wielded is swung about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A militant celebrity swinging a golf club or flat iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron' looks like a tool or golf club; it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron is one of the d-block elements in the periodic table, a typical example of this class.

clue.text: Group gathered round front of restaurant for meal

indicators.note: the group is gathered round, enclosing the next letter

parts.note: a bunch is a group

indicators.note: front of takes the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Diners clustered outside a restaurant waiting to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A late-morning meal combining breakfast and lunch.

clue.text: Prime requirement for bread, say?

parts.note: bread is traditionally spread with this dairy product first, before any topping

explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime' hints at priming a surface before painting: the first layer on a slice of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The dairy spread is the first thing put on a slice, as a primer goes on a wall.

clue.text: Superior navy vessel

parts.note: U is an abbreviation for upper-class, superior
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A top-quality naval ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship; it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A vase or container, such as one for ashes or tea, is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Pugnacious player at crease getting four — word of disapproval about that?

indicators.note: the exclamation is wrapped about the preceding pieces

parts.note: Come! is an exclamation of reproof
in cricket the batsman, or bat, stands at the crease
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A cricketer hits a boundary four and gets a scolding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about that' wraps the exclamation round the batsman and the numeral. A crease is the line a cricket batsman stands at; 'Come, come!' is a mild reproof.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone eager to fight or argue.

clue.text: I am surrounded by beastly noises from the rear — it's wind!

indicators.note: the words I am sit inside the animal noises
the cattle sounds are read from the back to the front

parts.note: moos are the sounds made by cows
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Someone surrounded by mooing cattle notices a smell of wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the rear' turns the cattle sounds into SOOM; the contraction sits inside, after the first letter. 'wind' suggests flatulence, but it is a desert gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot, dry, dust-laden wind of the Arabian and Saharan deserts.

clue.text: My nation is involved in a sort of contradiction

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A citizen notes that their country is caught up in a paradox.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy, a conflict between two laws or principles that each seem reasonable.

clue.text: Kiss Gregory?

definitions.meaning: a quick light kiss on the cheek
Gregory, surname of the Hollywood star of To Kill a Mockingbird

explanation.definitionFit: A brief kiss, and the surname of the American film actor Gregory.

clue.text: Old general — he's a dynamo in action

indicators.note: in action means moving about, so these letters are set in motion into a new order

explanation.surface: A tribute to an old general as a dynamo on the battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Israeli military commander and defence minister, famous for his eye patch.

clue.text: At last tour's on the move — there's a cloud high above

indicators.note: moving signals these letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: the letters of at last tours, the S of the apostrophe included

explanation.surface: A long-awaited tour finally gets going, under a high sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey or bluish sheet cloud at middle altitude, high in the sky.

clue.text: Purr, happy to be lower than the rest

parts.note: to hum is to purr, like an engine
blest, blessed, means happy or fortunate

explanation.surface: A contented cat purring beneath the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowest in rank or status, the superlative of meek or lowly.

clue.text: Girl having got hit is not embarrassed

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
bashed means hit

explanation.surface: A girl who has been hit is not ashamed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'is not embarrassed' with is as a link: the adjective means unashamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unashamed and composed; not abashed or disconcerted.

clue.text: Taunt the Yorkshire guy trying to be funny

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect the is shortened to t'
a wit is a person who makes jokes

explanation.surface: Mocking a Yorkshireman who fancies himself a comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease or ridicule someone, as a verb meaning to mock.

clue.text: Queen of France wants noise controlled

parts.note: reine is French for queen
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A French queen wanting the racket kept down.
explanation.definitionFit: Held back or restrained, as a horse is checked with the reins.

clue.text: County batsman who captained England gets duck

parts.note: Peter May was an English Test batsman and captain in the 1950s
in cricket a duck is a score of nought, O

explanation.surface: An England captain gets out for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish county in Connacht on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Shrub has nothing left by the daffodil season?

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
daffodils bloom in spring, around the Easter festival

explanation.surface: A garden plant left bare when the spring flowers come.
explanation.definitionFit: Also called Russian olive, a silvery-leaved bush or small tree.

clue.text: Town hospital before in France

parts.note: H is the sign for hospital
avant is French for before

explanation.surface: A hospital that preceded others in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in Hampshire, a county on England's south coast near Portsmouth.

clue.text: Game sponsor comes along with meat

parts.note: to back is to sponsor or support
gammon is cured ham

explanation.surface: A sponsor arrives bringing ham for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game for two played with counters and dice.

clue.text: Garment of honour supplied by king or queen

indicators.note: the honour is handed out by the monarch, so it follows

parts.note: R stands for rex or regina, king or queen
the OBE is a British honour, Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A ceremonial gown worn for an honour presented by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A long loose outer gown, often ceremonial.

clue.text: Slattern observed in Tube sometimes

indicators.note: the letters are seen lying within the following words

explanation.surface: An untidy woman spotted on the London Underground now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's Underground railway.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern English dialect the broom word is also a scornful term for a slovenly woman.

clue.text: Insect ruins that wine

indicators.note: ruins means wrecks, so these letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A bug gets into the wine and spoils it.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the termite, a pale wood-eating social insect.

clue.text: This cardinal will bring up anything

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up means writing the letters from the bottom

parts.note: owt is northern English dialect for anything

explanation.surface: A churchman who will vomit anything at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a prelate; it is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal number, the counting number after one.

clue.text: Daughter facing English exam shows hate

parts.note: a test is an exam

explanation.surface: A daughter sitting her English paper loathes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe intensely; a strong synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Skilful mediator managed to get me off

indicators.note: the letters are managed, handled into a new arrangement, once the other word is taken away

explanation.surface: A clever go-between who got the speaker out of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get me off' removes M and E; 'managed' rearranges DIATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever and deft with the hands or mind.

clue.text: Lacking a chum to advance money, you'd say?

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, signalling a homophone

parts.note: to loan some, lending some cash

explanation.surface: A friendless person asks someone to lend them cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonely; without companions or friends.
